oil.summary: Crude markets sent mixed signals today. WTI surged 2.98% to $102.88/bbl on a third consecutive weekly draw in US inventories (-1.9 mb per EIA) and persistent Gulf supply disruption, with at least 50 tankers reported stuck in the Gulf. Brent, however, slipped 1.87% to $111.73 despite UBS raising its year-end Brent target to $110, suggesting some profit-taking after a 15% monthly WTI rally. Distillates softened, with Heating Oil off 2.13% and RBOB down 0.93%. The geopolitical backdrop remains combustible: Iran is reportedly budgeting for $130 oil in 2027, while Chinese refiners pivot to West African and Brazilian barrels as freight eases. PetroChina posted a 21.6% Q3 profit jump citing war-inflated prices. Options markets price a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the May 2027 meeting.
drivers: US crude inventories fell 1.9 mb for the week ending Oct 23, providing floor support for WTI
Gulf shipping crisis keeps at least 50 tankers idle; tanker giant Bahri posted a tenfold Q3 profit surge on surging rates
Geopolitical risk premium elevated: Iran targets $130 oil in 2027 budget; Ukraine-Russia energy infrastructure strikes ongoing; Trump-Russia diesel deal under Western scrutiny

gas.summary: Natural gas markets staged a sharp rally across both benchmarks. Henry Hub jumped 12.46% to $3.035/MMBtu in a single session, extending a weekly gain of 8.71%. TTF surged 4.00% to €99.9/MWh, now up 43% over the past month — a striking move heading into winter. The most significant catalyst is QatarEnergy's extension of its LNG force majeure through end-2026, removing key term supply certainty for European and Asian buyers at a critical seasonal juncture. Russia is simultaneously offering China a substantial gas discount, reflecting Moscow's fiscal dependence on Beijing. Equinor, benefiting from high prices, tripled Q3 adjusted net income and raised its 2026 production growth forecast to ~4%, while PetroChina also cited war-inflated gas prices as a profit driver.
drivers: QatarEnergy extended LNG force majeure to end-2026, stripping European and Asian buyers of guaranteed term supply heading into winter
TTF +43% on the month reflects acute European supply anxiety; Henry Hub +12.46% today signals US market tightening
Russia offering China a large gas discount underscores Kremlin's leverage loss, while Equinor raised output guidance on strong commodity prices

power.summary: EU carbon edged up 1.14% to $84.78/EUA, building on a 4% weekly and nearly 4% monthly gain, as elevated TTF at €99.9/MWh keeps gas-fired generation expensive and sustains carbon cost pass-through. The geopolitical backdrop is directly pressuring power infrastructure: a drone attack on a UAE nuclear power plant pushed oil to a two-week high earlier today, and Ukraine launched over 1,000 drones striking a Russian oil terminal in St. Petersburg. Iran's deepening nuclear entanglement — now turning to Russia for nuclear power as IAEA oversight falters — adds a longer-term proliferation overhang to regional energy security. On the structural side, China's wind and solar capacity surpassed 2 terawatts, a landmark that may gradually reshape global carbon dynamics. Gulf states are reported to be negotiating a regional peace deal covering Hormuz, Yemen, and Iran's nuclear program.
drivers: QatarEnergy LNG force majeure and TTF at €99.9/MWh sustain high carbon prices as gas generation costs remain elevated
Drone attack on UAE nuclear plant and Ukraine's 1,000-drone strike on Russian energy infrastructure highlight escalating power and energy security risks
China's wind and solar capacity crosses 2 TW milestone; Gulf states in peace talks covering Strait of Hormuz and Iran nuclear program signal potential medium-term supply normalization
